## Architecture Guidance Metadata

```yaml
guidance_id: 'GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-<PHASE>.D.NN'
guidance_name: '<Name>'
guidance_type: 'architecture-building-block'
abb_type: '<composite / component>'
# Composite ABBs only — list all Component ABB GUIDs; omit entirely for Component ABBs:
# child_abbs:
#   - 'GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-2.D.01'
#   - 'GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-2.D.02'
adm_phase: 'Phase B-D'
parent_abb: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-ABB-1.D.NN — omit for Composite ABBs>'
parent_vision: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-VISION-0.D.NN>'
realized_by_sbbs: []  # Intentionally empty — SBBs are Phase E-F outputs authored using sbb-template.md
paired_rad: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-RAD-3.D.NN — Component ABBs only; omit for Composite>'
paired_bdd: '<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-BDD-3.5.D.NN — Component ABBs only; omit for Composite>'
category: '<application | business | infrastructure | information | technology | itsm-operations | governance>'
version: '0.1.0'
status: 'draft'
applicability: '<enterprise | domain | project | component>'
tags: ['<domain>', '<capability-tag>', 'architecture-building-block', '<abb-type>']
author: '<Author Name>'
```

> **Before authoring this ABB**: verify the Architecture Vision (`GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-VISION-0.D.NN`) exists at `draft` status or higher. For Component ABBs, also verify the parent Composite ABB exists. See `togaf-artifact-creation-guidelines.md` §2.0 in the same artifacts template directory — update this path when copying this template to its production location.

[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md#normative-language-convention]

### Normative Language Convention

> **Authoring note — choose ONE pattern based on ABB type:**
>
> **Composite ABB**: include the full RFC 2119 table below. This section is defined once for the entire hierarchy and all Component ABBs inherit it by reference.
>
> **Component ABB**: replace this entire section with a single-line reference back to the Vision: `Per [<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-VISION-0.D.NN> §Normative Language Convention](<relative-path-to-vision>.md): **SHALL** = mandatory; **SHOULD** = strongly recommended; **MAY** = optional.`

This document and all Component ABBs in this hierarchy use normative language per RFC 2119:

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **SHALL** | Mandatory — absolute obligation |
| **SHALL NOT** | Mandatory prohibition |
| **SHOULD** | Strongly recommended — deviation requires documented justification |
| **SHOULD NOT** | Strongly discouraged — deviation requires documented justification |
| **MAY** | Optional — permitted but not required |

> **Exception and Waiver Process**: Teams that cannot meet a SHALL requirement must submit a risk acceptance or waiver request through the established enterprise governance process. Waivers require documented justification and approval from the appropriate architecture authority. Temporary waivers must include a remediation timeline.

[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md#capability-requirements]

## Capability Requirements

> **Authoring note**: Every requirement in this section MUST be uniquely identifiable using the label format `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<SEQ>` (e.g., `REQ-APP-AUTH-001`). This label is used in the BDD Specification to trace Given/When/Then scenarios back to individual requirements. Do not omit labels — unlabeled requirements cannot be tested.
page_texts.9:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md#shall-requirements]

### SHALL Requirements

These requirements are **mandatory**. Every SHALL requirement MUST map to at least one Given/When/Then scenario in the paired BDD Specification.

| Req ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-001` | The capability SHALL <mandatory requirement 1> |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-002` | The capability SHALL <mandatory requirement 2> |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-003` | The capability SHALL NOT <mandatory prohibition> |
page_texts.10:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md#should-requirements]

### SHOULD Requirements

These requirements are **strongly recommended**. Deviations must be documented and justified. SHOULD requirements SHOULD have at least one Given/When/Then scenario tagged `@recommended` in the BDD Specification.

| Req ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-010` | The capability SHOULD <strongly recommended requirement 1> |
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-011` | The capability SHOULD <strongly recommended requirement 2> |
page_texts.11:
[resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md#may-requirements]

### MAY Requirements

These requirements are **optional**. They represent permitted behaviors or configurations that the capability may choose to implement.

| Req ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `REQ-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-020` | The capability MAY <optional requirement 1> |

## Interface Contracts

## Behavioral Contract Summary

> This section provides a human-readable summary of the behaviors that BDD Specification scenarios must validate. Detailed Given/When/Then scenarios are in the paired BDD Specification document.
>
> **Full BDD Specification**: [<GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-BDD-3.5.D.NN> — <Name> BDD Specification](<relative-path-to-bdd>.md)

| Behavior | Priority | Req IDs |
|---|---|---|
| <Described behavior — what happens under normal conditions> | SHALL | `REQ-...-001`, `REQ-...-002` |
| <Described behavior — what happens under error conditions> | SHALL | `REQ-...-003` |
| <Described behavior — recommended pattern> | SHOULD | `REQ-...-010` |
